newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO court sends Arafat guard to death for treason.
newsitem.headline: PLO court sends Arafat guard to death for treason.

text.p: A PLO military court sentenced a member of Yasser Arafat's presidential guard to death and two other guards to long prison sentences on Tuesday for treason and collaboration with Israel, witnesses said.
The three were arrested last month and charged with terrorising, abducting and killing Palestinians on orders from a "foreign country".
The three guards admitted to the crimes but their lawyers said later investigators used force to extract confessions.
The court sentenced a fourth man who was not a member of the presidential guard to five years in prison for similar charges.
Witnesses identified the guard sentenced to death as Fawzi Sawalha, 21. His laywer said he would appeal the sentence.
Collaboration with Israel is still considered treason among Palestinians despite the signing of the 1993 peace deal between the PLO and Israel.

PLO security officials said since self-rule was established in 1994, Palestinian police had detained tens of collaborators and that many have fled PLO-ruled areas for safety in Israel. Three Palestinian land dealers, considered collaborators for selling Arab land to Israelis, have recently been killed in mysterious circumstances.
Prosecutor general Ahmed Buraq said the four were charged after complaints were filed against them by eight Palestinians from the Asira al-Shamaliyah village, north of Nablus.
The guards' relatives condemned the court's decision as "oppression."
"This is a harsh sentence. Khaldoun is innocent...he wasn't involved in criminal acts," said Sulafa Yassin, 40, aunt of Khaldoun Asamneh, 24, who was given a life sentence.
It was the second time a military court imposed the death penalty on Palestinian security officers.
Last month a PLO military court in self-ruled Gaza sentenced three PLO officers to death by firing squad for killing a man held in custody by an elite unit that guards Arafat.
None of the death sentences has been carried out.
Arafat has ordered several security officers jailed for human rights violations and for disobeying orders since he took control of parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip in 1994.
The Palestinian Authority has been under fire from human rights organisations for alleged violations. The groups say at least 14 Palestinians have died in custody since the start of Palestinian rule.
